items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well the only thing -- only mason I thought he was from Chicago was somebody told me he used to play sort of like intermission inhibition piano at the Grand Terrace. [INTERVIEWEE] Maybe he did.

ctx.x: It is, true. We was [crossed out] there.

"Didn't he they do Ramble." They It's kind of a mockery because it's -- used to play that thing coming back from the funeral-- the "Free as the cemetery, (unintelligible) birds", like that, you know, because we used to -- years ago in New York, had like the big person was -- had died, like Mason or Odd- fellows. They don't have those funerals up and down the streets anymore in New York like they did years ago. They don't have them anymore. Mostly they do the thing at the temple or at the big funeral parlor. Even…

Yeah, well, there's a funny thing about that. I mean there is the New Orleans thing, and then there is like some of the funeral services they have in churches here, where people get up -- I mean you've been to some of them, and they sing and they play, and it's almost as though they were doing an audition.
